question: For each integer \(N\gt1,\) define positive integers to be congruent if they leave the same nonnegative remainder when divided by \(N.\) If \(69,\) \(90,\) and \(125\) are congruent in one such system, then in that same system, \(81\) is congruent to:
solution:
When two integers have the same remainder upon division by \(N\), subtracting them cancels that remainder. Their difference must therefore be a multiple of \(N\).

Thus \(N\) divides both
\[90-69=21\qquad\text{and}\qquad125-90=35.\]
The positive common divisors of \(21\) and \(35\) are \(1\) and \(7\). Since \(N>1\), we must have \(N=7\). This works: \(69\), \(90\), and \(125\) each leave remainder \(6\) when divided by \(7\).

Finally,
\[81=11\cdot7+4,\]
so \(81\) is congruent to \(\boxed{4}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

nodes.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.* Examples: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known.
